 “My kids are not thugs. They’re not gangsters. They’re here getting educated.” Mickey Joseph apologizes for postgame fight, defends players 
 14 G-men suspended after the fight with the school being fined $25,000 
 By Aaron Dietrich and Zac Berger Published : Nov. 11, 2026 at 11:32 AM CST Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google MONROE, La. (KNOE) - Grambling football is dealing with the fallout from the postgame brwal with Arkansas-Pine Bluff.
 12 players have been suspended this week and two others are out for the rest of the season. The school was also fined $25,000.
 The disciplinary action comes after Grambling’s third straight loss.
 Head Coach Mickey Joseph apologized for the incident and said the program wants to prevent it from happening again.
 “My kids are not thugs. They’re not gangsters. They’re here getting educated,” Joseph said. “I’m always going to defend my kids. I’m never going to stand back and not defend them because they’re doing something that a lot of kids are not doing. They’re in school getting educated.”
 Mickey looks for his squad to move forward as they enter into the final two weeks of the season.
 “They made a mistake. I made a mistake. We said we’re sorry,” Joseph said. “We’re going to play football and we’re going to do what we came here to do. And we just like to say it again, we apologize.”
